# Invariants

<!-- Generated by scripts/src/bin/invariants.rs from the code: edit the doc comment there, then run `write`. -->

What blaze's code promises, stated once, beside the test that checks it. Each is a doc comment
opening `/// The invariant:`, `/// The refinement:` or `/// The reference model:`; an invariant or a
refinement counts only with a control in its file, a test that plants a bug its oracle must
catch. A change to this file in a pull request is a promise added, reworded or dropped.

149 invariants, 21 refinements, 12 reference models.
By level: 125 tested, 44 simulated, 1 model-checked, 0 proved.

## Invariants

### base-db

- **`a_process_variable_nothing_reads_changes_no_row`** *tested* (`crates/base-db/src/tests.rs`): a change of a process variable nothing reads changes no row. A query that reads `FOO` reads `FOO`'s own memo; with `UNRELATED` changed, added or removed, the walk from the variables written verifies that one memo, finds it equal and stops: 0 rows changed, so nothing that read `FOO` runs again.
  Controls: `a_read_variable_that_changed`.

### blaze-cargo

- **`a_run_asks_the_daemon_for_no_summary_of_its_build`** *tested* (`crates/blaze-cargo/src/cli/observe.rs`): a `run` waits for nothing between its build's answer and its program. Where the answer does not carry why the build recomputed, a `run` says nothing of it and asks nothing; a build asks. The control is the build's row: with `ask` the daemon is the source, so the `run`'s `Nowhere` is the flag's doing.
- **`the_thin_blaze_sends_this_clis_request_byte_for_byte`** *tested* (`crates/blaze-cargo/src/cli/tests.rs`): for every command line the thin `blaze` sends itself (blaze-thin's `route`), its request is this CLI's, byte for byte in the API's deterministic CBOR, and it runs the program with the arguments this CLI's parser gives it. So the daemon builds one thing whichever sent it, and the engine can go on with an answer the thin `blaze` began (`resume`, which refuses any other request).
- **`the_thin_blaze_prints_a_plain_answer_as_this_cli_does`** *tested* (`crates/blaze-cargo/src/cli/tests.rs`): what the thin `blaze` prints of an answer it takes as plain (blaze-thin's `answer`) is what this CLI prints of the same responses, and the program it runs is the one this CLI runs, from the same directory with the same arguments and variables. Anything it does not take as plain it hands to this CLI, so the two never print one answer two ways.
- **`a_cgroups_footprint_is_its_charge_less_the_file_cache_the_kernel_can_drop`** *tested* (`crates/blaze-cargo/src/raw/memory.rs`): the cgroup's footprint is its charge less the file cache the kernel can drop, and nothing else is taken off. The directed case: a cgroup of 10 GiB of which 6 are file cache, 1 of that shared memory, is 5 GiB (the control: counting all of `file` as droppable says 4, counting none says 10). A line that only begins with a field's name (`file_mapped`, `shmem_thp`) is not the field.
  Controls: `shared_memory_dropped_and_file_cache_kept`.
- **`a_provided_run_is_answered_the_same_randomness_every_time`** *tested* (`crates/blaze-cargo/src/sandbox/linux.rs`): in a run given a provider, what a process gets from `getrandom` and from `/dev/urandom` is the provider's: the same bytes on every run of the same seed, other bytes for each process and each open, other bytes under another seed, and nothing in the trace that can't be traced.
  Controls: `randomness_read_without_a_provider`, `an_allocation_that_seeds_in_the_window`.
- **`the_launchers_window_makes_no_call_the_supervisor_sees`** *tested* (`crates/blaze-cargo/src/sandbox/linux.rs`): between its filter's install and its exec the launcher's child makes no call the supervisor notes or answers (no allocation that seeds a heap, no clock): the supervisor takes every call of that process for the program's, and an answered one would move the program's stream.
  Controls: `randomness_read_without_a_provider`, `an_allocation_that_seeds_in_the_window`.
- **`the_work_between_requests_waits_for_quiet_turns_after_the_answer`** *simulated* (`crates/blaze-cargo/src/serve/daemon.rs`): the work between requests (the collections, the image's making, in line on the loop) first runs [`QUIET_BEFORE_BETWEEN`] quiet turns after a build's answer, however long the build turned with nothing completing: the client that got the answer asks its next thing (its rows, why it recomputed) into an idle loop. - **`a_kept_answer_is_said_again_only_while_a_walk_would_say_the_same`** *tested* (`crates/blaze-cargo/src/serve/job/noop/tests.rs`): the lane says a kept answer again only when a walk of every unit would say the same of the state the request is asked in, with every output in place and no other job under way: no input a build reads changed since the answer was kept. - **`a_builds_rows_are_flushed_only_after_its_answer`** *tested* (`crates/blaze-cargo/src/serve/observe.rs`): a build's rows reach no file of the history until its answer was said ([`ToHistory::Answered`]), whatever else is flushed meanwhile; its misses are explained and told as it ends, before that. So the answer of a build never shares the disk with the flush of its own profile. The history's thread is given the build's end and then a reader's flush: once that is told, nothing of the build is on disk. Then its answer and a second reader's flush behind it: its row is there. - **`a_write_at_an_offset_goes_through_the_page_cache`** *simulated* (`crates/blaze-core/src/uring.rs`): a write at an offset goes through the page cache whatever its size and alignment, so it completes without waiting for a device. Writes of 8 MiB at multiples of 8 MiB (a linked image's runs, as an edit's output is placed) and one unaligned: the open of each asks for no `O_DIRECT`, each is one buffered write on its slot, and each reads back as written. Its control is `the_oracle_catches_a_write_at_an_offset_opened_around_the_cache`.
  Controls: `a_write_at_an_offset_opened_around_the_cache`.
- **`every_public_wait_ends_in_a_sandboxed_process`** *tested* (`crates/blaze-core/src/wait/filtered.rs`): in a process the sandbox launcher marked, under a filter that refuses io_uring as the sandbox's does, every wait `blaze_core::wait` gives ends, on the direct driver, and no ring is asked for.

- **`every_wait_ends_by_its_deadline_under_interruption`** *simulated* (`crates/blaze-core/src/wait/tests.rs`): whatever interrupts it, every wait ends by its deadline, never says it passed before it did, and is ready whenever its event came first.
  Controls: `a_retry_with_the_first_timeout`, `a_lost_wakeup`, `a_reaped_child_never_reported`, `a_lost_wakeup_through_the_direct_driver`, `a_reaped_child_never_reported_through_the_direct_driver`.
- **`no_unpark_is_lost_under_interruption`** *simulated* (`crates/blaze-core/src/wait/tests.rs`): whatever interrupts it and whenever its unpark comes, no wakeup is lost and every park ends by its deadline.
  Controls: `a_retry_with_the_first_timeout`, `a_lost_wakeup`, `a_reaped_child_never_reported`, `a_lost_wakeup_through_the_direct_driver`, `a_reaped_child_never_reported_through_the_direct_driver`.
- **`every_reaped_child_is_reported_under_interruption`** *simulated* (`crates/blaze-core/src/wait/tests.rs`): whatever interrupts the wait and whenever the child exits, every child is reaped once and its exit reported, by the reap's deadline or after it.
  Controls: `a_retry_with_the_first_timeout`, `a_lost_wakeup`, `a_reaped_child_never_reported`, `a_lost_wakeup_through_the_direct_driver`, `a_reaped_child_never_reported_through_the_direct_driver`.
- **`no_unpark_is_lost_through_the_direct_driver`** *simulated* (`crates/blaze-core/src/wait/tests.rs`): on the direct driver (a futex wait to an absolute time on the kernel's clock, made anew for every call), whatever interrupts it and whenever its unpark comes, no wakeup is lost and every park ends by its deadline.
  Controls: `a_retry_with_the_first_timeout`, `a_lost_wakeup`, `a_reaped_child_never_reported`, `a_lost_wakeup_through_the_direct_driver`, `a_reaped_child_never_reported_through_the_direct_driver`.
- **`every_reaped_child_is_reported_through_the_direct_driver`** *simulated* (`crates/blaze-core/src/wait/tests.rs`): on the direct driver (a look with `waitid`, a poll of the child's pidfd, the look again, then the reap), whatever interrupts the wait and whenever the child exits, every child is reaped once and its exit reported, by the reap's deadline or after it.
  Controls: `a_retry_with_the_first_timeout`, `a_lost_wakeup`, `a_reaped_child_never_reported`, `a_lost_wakeup_through_the_direct_driver`, `a_reaped_child_never_reported_through_the_direct_driver`.

  Controls: `an_ack_for_a_generation_not_collected_for`, `a_leave_that_keeps_its_ack`.
- **`frames_after_a_build_hold_at_most_the_warm_shelf_a_worker`** *tested* (`crates/blaze-mem/src/tests.rs`): once a build's tasks have all ended, the frame memory each of its worker threads still holds is at most [`frame::WARM`], whatever the tasks held, however they nested and in whatever order they ran; nothing else of the frames outlives them. What does outlive a build is a named owner's (here a [`Frame`] of the test's, standing for a cache), and its bytes are its own count, unchanged by the tasks. A build-shaped run: four workers, each a seeded sequence of tasks of the sizes a build's are, nested up to three deep, then one of twice the bound. The control: the same reading sees the memory while it is held (each worker's measured peak is at least its largest task's scratch, far past the bound), so a bound that holds after is not a reading that sees nothing. The directed case: twelve tasks nested, each holding a span of 8 MiB at once, more spans than a shelf keeps and 96 MiB together; the thread still ends within the bound.

### blaze-query

- **`a_merged_log_names_every_node_it_named_before_from_every_view`** *tested* (`crates/blaze-query/src/db/frontier.rs`): merging the log's oldest findings loses no name. A host that asks from any view, the views before the merged findings too, is named every node it was named before the merge (it may be named more), so no host is ever told the log cannot answer and left to sweep everything it holds.
  Controls: `a_log_that_drops_its_oldest_findings`.
- **`a_decoded_id_is_its_word_and_a_refused_word_is_no_id`** *tested* (`crates/blaze-query/src/db/tests.rs`): `Id::decode`'s contract, for any word: an ID it gives is the word it was given, and a word it refuses is 0 or past `Id::MAX_U32`, so no word decodes to another ID and none to an ID no storage could give. Words are drawn around the bounds as well as anywhere in 64 bits.
- **`the_changed_set_names_every_row_whose_value_differs_from_a_run_from_scratch`** *tested* (`crates/blaze-query/src/db/tests/changed.rs`): `changed_since(V) ⊇ { k : value_now(k) ≠ value_at(V, k) }` over the keys made by `V`, and every key it names more is one whose value moved in some view between (a change and a change back); with no untracked read, no eviction and one walk a view it equals the set. Checked against a from-scratch evaluation after every step of a random program and edit sequence.
  Controls: `a_reverse_edge_not_recorded`, `a_stale_edge_after_a_rows_dependencies_change`, `a_changed_reader_that_does_not_pass_the_walk_on`, `a_cutoff_not_applied`, `an_evicted_row_passed_over`, `a_walk_that_runs_a_levels_rows`, `a_walk_that_contains_every_unwind`.
- **`a_level_under_the_walks_serial_bound_is_verified_on_the_walkers_thread`** *tested* (`crates/blaze-query/src/db/tests/changed.rs`): a walk's level of fewer rows than its serial bound is verified on the walker's thread, every row, with no job handed to the pool: an edit's levels cost no dispatch. 50 readers of one input, more than the small-loop predictor's 32 and fewer than the walk's 64: each runs again on the thread that asked for the changed set. Asked from a thread of no pool, so a row handed to the pool would run on a worker, never here.
  Controls: `a_reverse_edge_not_recorded`, `a_stale_edge_after_a_rows_dependencies_change`, `a_changed_reader_that_does_not_pass_the_walk_on`, `a_cutoff_not_applied`, `an_evicted_row_passed_over`, `a_walk_that_runs_a_levels_rows`, `a_walk_that_contains_every_unwind`.
- **`a_wide_level_is_marked_and_no_row_of_it_runs_in_the_walk`** *tested* (`crates/blaze-query/src/db/tests/changed.rs`): a walk that meets a wide level runs no row and waits for none. From that level on it marks: each row it reaches is named as changed and left to whoever asks for it, so a change the whole program reads costs the walk its reverse edges, where a level handed to the pool a job a row had its jobs wait on each other for minutes (2026-11-11). 100 readers of one input, each read by a row of its own: the walk runs none of the 200, names all, and a row asked for afterwards is run then and answers as the model.
  Controls: `a_reverse_edge_not_recorded`, `a_stale_edge_after_a_rows_dependencies_change`, `a_changed_reader_that_does_not_pass_the_walk_on`, `a_cutoff_not_applied`, `an_evicted_row_passed_over`, `a_walk_that_runs_a_levels_rows`, `a_walk_that_contains_every_unwind`.
- **`a_walk_contains_at_most_eight_unwinds_and_marks_the_rest`** *tested* (`crates/blaze-query/src/db/tests/changed.rs`): one walk contains the unwinding of at most 8 verifications (rule 18); the rows it reaches after that are marked, not run, and every row is still named as changed. Of 40 rows whose runs panic, 8 are run and 32 marked.
  Controls: `a_reverse_edge_not_recorded`, `a_stale_edge_after_a_rows_dependencies_change`, `a_changed_reader_that_does_not_pass_the_walk_on`, `a_cutoff_not_applied`, `an_evicted_row_passed_over`, `a_walk_that_runs_a_levels_rows`, `a_walk_that_contains_every_unwind`.
- **`a_small_loop_runs_every_task_on_its_calling_thread`** *tested* (`crates/blaze-query/src/db/tests/small.rs`): a loop of at most [`SMALL_ITEMS`] tasks whose site predicts under [`SMALL_NS`] runs every task on the calling thread, in order, and submits no job: the site counts it as run here. A site with no run yet predicts no cost, so an edit's first loop is here.
- **`a_stale_head_of_another_tasks_cycle_is_waited_for_never_run`** *tested* (`crates/blaze-query/src/db/tests/stale_head.rs`): a provisional row is run and written only by the task whose stack holds its cycle's head. A task that comes to hold the flight of a stale inner head of another task's cycle waits for the head instead, so every task gets the fixpoint a single task computes, and no run finds its own row emptied under it.

- **`a_restored_image_names_only_what_it_holds`** *model-checked* (`crates/blaze-query/src/tests.rs`): a database restored from an image holds no record that names a memo, an edge or bytes of the blob the image lacks: each is refused as the image is opened, naming the section and the record, never met by the first request that reads it. - **`a_restored_database_answers_as_a_warm_one_and_a_fresh_one`** *simulated* (`crates/blaze-query/src/tests/restore.rs`): after any run of edits, asks, images placed, settles, power cuts at any effect of a placing and starts, a database restored from the image's file answers every key as a warm database and a fresh one do, which is what the files give; the file is always one image whole (the one placed, or the one before it); a start refuses no image that only the power touched and restores no other blaze's; and with one byte of the file changed, every answer is still the files' or a typed refusal, never a panic. `HEGEL_TEST_CASES=<n>` runs it longer.

- **`a_memo_made_by_other_code_is_never_read_as_this_codes`** *simulated* (`crates/blaze-query/src/tests/restore.rs`): a memo is the result of the code that made it and of no other (version skew, two builds of one query over one image): a blaze whose query has another producer restores the image and runs the query, never reading the older code's value as its own.
  Controls: `a_restored_memo_used_after_its_input_changed`, `an_image_committed_before_its_bytes_are_durable`, `code_changed_under_one_producer`.

- **`a_directory_never_passes_its_quota`** *tested* (`crates/blaze-std/src/tests/budget.rs`): a `Dir` with a quota never passes it and spends it exactly. The lengths of the files on the simulated disk fit the quota; a write that does not fit is a typed `Over` and writes nothing.

- **`cancelling_a_scope_ends_its_waits_with_cancelled`** *tested* (`crates/blaze-std/src/tests/cancel.rs`): cancelling a scope ends its waits with `Stopped::Cancelled`. - **`closing_a_file_syncs_it_or_says_why_not`** *simulated* (`crates/blaze-std/src/tests/close.rs`): a `File::close_synced` that returned `Ok` has made the file and every append durable (a crash right after keeps them all), and one whose flush the disk fails returns that failure, op `Close`, never `Ok`.

- **`a_child_context_never_has_a_later_deadline`** *tested* (`crates/blaze-std/src/tests/contexts.rs`): a child `Cx` never has a later deadline than its parent. Whatever tree of `until`, `span`, scopes and tasks grows from the root, each context's deadline is at or before the one it was made from.

- **`provenance_records_the_calls_made`** *tested* (`crates/blaze-std/src/tests/eval.rs`): the graph `Provenance` writes holds exactly the calls made, each under the call whose body made it, in order.

### blaze-storemodel

- **`what_is_kept_after_an_answer_survives_any_crash_and_no_lost_value_is_served`** *tested* (`crates/blaze-storemodel/src/tests.rs`): an answer may be sent on results not yet durable; nothing derived from that answer is reused across a crash unless its tickets were durable. After any crash the restore serves no value whose bytes were lost, holds everything the store called durable and everything an answered build kept, and every answer's settling ended kept or said lost. Two builds on shared and separate keys with a reader, and a snapshot beside a build, each build answering before it flushes: every schedule, a crash after every IO step, so at every point between an answer sent and its results durable; with an IO failure anywhere, so a settling that ends with the store stopped. Then two kernel gets of one identity in two worlds racing for one shape slot, each answering at once and keeping what it left once it and every store before it is durable, with an IO failure anywhere and effects completing in any order.
  Controls: `a_kept_answer_relied_on_before_its_tickets_were_durable`, `a_settling_failure_dropped_silently`.

- **`a_body_edit_touches_only_what_reads_the_body`** *tested* (`crates/hir/src/check/bodies/tests.rs`): a warm edit of one function's body costs every stage a constant that does not grow with the workspace. - **`a_proc_macro_under_an_attribute_macro_names_its_expander_once_its_crate_is_given_its_macros`** *tested* (`crates/hir-def/src/nameres/delta/tests.rs`): a proc-macro crate given its macros names the expander of each in its map, the one its root file declares and the one an attribute macro's expansion declares (alloy-sol-macro's `#[proc_macro] #[proc_macro_error] pub fn sol`): the crate's map is read before its module is built, when no macro of it has an expander, and resolves again when the list is given.
  Controls: `a_given_crate_whose_root_runs_again_only_for_its_log`, `a_crate_above_a_written_one_left_without_a_job`, `an_edit_of_a_crate_root_that_changes_a_scope`, `an_include_whose_file_is_not_kept`.
- **`a_write_of_a_file_has_a_job_for_its_crate_and_those_above_it_alone`** *tested* (`crates/hir-def/src/nameres/delta/tests.rs`): a crate with no job in a write (`delta::unreached`) is one whose job would change nothing, so after any write every crate's maintained map is the one a fresh resolution makes (`check_db`). And the cost: a write of a file has a job for its crate and the crates above it alone, not one for every crate of the graph.
  Controls: `a_given_crate_whose_root_runs_again_only_for_its_log`, `a_crate_above_a_written_one_left_without_a_job`, `an_edit_of_a_crate_root_that_changes_a_scope`, `an_include_whose_file_is_not_kept`.
- **`a_body_edit_in_a_crate_root_whose_children_export_macros_sets_no_scope`** *tested* (`crates/hir-def/src/nameres/delta/tests.rs`): an edit inside one function's body sets no module's scope and no field of its crate's resolution, in the crate root's file as in any other and whatever the root's children export to its textual scope: a body binds no name of a module. On ripgrep 2026-11-10 a one-line edit of `rg::main` wrote 25 `ScopeInput`s, and 841 `ScopeInput::name` and 833 `ScopeInput::legacy_macro` ran again for them, which every body of the crate then verified through.
  Controls: `a_given_crate_whose_root_runs_again_only_for_its_log`, `a_crate_above_a_written_one_left_without_a_job`, `an_edit_of_a_crate_root_that_changes_a_scope`, `an_include_whose_file_is_not_kept`.
- **`a_crate_that_includes_a_file_has_a_job_for_that_file_and_not_for_another_crates`** *tested* (`crates/hir-def/src/nameres/delta/tests.rs`): a crate that expanded an `include!` has a job in a write only when the write holds a file one of its logs or expansions read: the file its `include!` parsed, not any file it does not define. So an edit of a crate above it gives it no job and sets nothing of it, and a write of the included file still reaches it: after either, every crate's maintained map is the one a fresh resolution makes (`check_db`).
  Controls: `a_given_crate_whose_root_runs_again_only_for_its_log`, `a_crate_above_a_written_one_left_without_a_job`, `an_edit_of_a_crate_root_that_changes_a_scope`, `an_include_whose_file_is_not_kept`.
- **`records_are_equal_exactly_when_their_field_sets_are`** *tested* (`crates/hir-def/src/record.rs`): two record types are equal exactly when their (name, type) sets are.
  Controls: `field_order_in_the_key`, `a_default_in_the_type_identity`.

### hir-ty

- **`a_flush_keeps_two_shapes_of_one_base_key`** *tested* (`crates/hir-ty/src/body_store/tests.rs`): every step a flush is given is kept, whatever else the same flush holds; two shapes of one base key take two slots, in a store that shows no put before its driver made it. Until 2026-11-10 the second shape was placed against the store alone, found slot 0 free, and was refused by the put the first had buffered ("keeping the shape of the MIR of StaticId(..): two images were made under .."), which lost everything the build left for the store and its front end with it: every build of ripgrep, whose crates have statics and functions alike but for their names.
  Controls: `a_flush_that_forgets_what_it_placed`.

### hir-ty-codegen

- **`many_threads_name_each_target_once`** *tested* (`crates/hir-ty-codegen/target.rs`): a triple names one target for good, whichever threads name it first and whatever else is named beside it ([`one_target_a_triple`]); one triple more than the table holds is refused by name, and a triple blaze emits no code for takes no slot.
  Controls: `a_target_made_at_each_look`.
- **`a_block_of_more_values_than_wasm_has_locals_runs_and_computes_what_its_ir_says`** *tested* (`crates/hir-ty-codegen/wasm.rs`): a function of more values than a WebAssembly function may have locals (50 000) is lowered to a body an engine takes, and it computes what its IR says: a value read only in its own block gives its local back after its last read, so the body's locals are as many as are live at once, not as many as there are values. sha2's unrolled `compress_block`, in rust-embed-impl's module, was refused by Wasmtime ("too many locals") when each value had a local of its own.
  Controls: `a_local_kept_for_every_value`.

### hir-ty-lean

- **`fnv1a_from_is_the_fold_of_its_bytes`** *tested* (`crates/hir-ty-lean/src/tests.rs`): the ledger's checksum loop `fnv1a_from` never panics (no index out of bounds, no counter overflow) and returns FNV-1a's fold of the seed over the bytes, for every seed and every slice. The proof is of the model this test holds to the tree's source: the function's text is read from crates/blaze-graph/src/ledger.rs, its emitted Lean must be the checked-in module the proof imports, and its structured MIR runs to the same fold on the inputs here. Lean 4.20.0 accepts the proof of the model (crates/blaze-graph/lean/BlazeGraph/Ledger.lean) and a proof is written that the model is what the function's MIR runs to (BlazeGraph/LedgerMir.lean, objective V7). This statement says `(proved: ..)` once three things hold on one commit, never before: this test and `fnv1a_from_is_embedded_as_the_body_its_proof_walks` pass (the model and the embedded body are what blaze emits), and `lake build` of `lean/` passes in the gate with both proofs.
  Controls: `a_continue_made_a_break`, `an_else_branch_dropped_at_a_join`, `an_xor_made_an_add`.

### hir-ty-mir

- **`early_drops_keep_every_program_as_rust_runs_it`** *tested* (`crates/hir-ty-mir/src/mir/early_drop/frontier.rs`): under early drop no local is dropped while a loan of it is live, no local is used after its drop, every initialized local is dropped exactly once on every path, the locals of one edge drop in scope order, and a scoped local drops where Rust drops it.
  Controls: `a_drop_before_the_last_use_of_a_reborrow`, `a_conditional_move_with_no_drop_flag`, `a_scoped_guard_dropped_early`, `two_locals_dropped_in_hash_order`.
- **`the_walk_agrees_with_the_reference_model`** *tested* (`crates/hir-ty-mir/src/tests/consteval/reach.rs`): for a random program of structs whose fields are plain, boxed, in a `Vec`, behind a counted or weak pointer, in a cell or in a generic struct, in any nesting and recursion, the walk clears a struct for the cycle question exactly when the reference model ([`model_is_acyclic`]) finds no way for a value of it to own itself.
  Controls: `a_shared_pointer_inside_an_option_in_a_cell_missed`, `a_box_recursion_taken_for_a_cycle`, `a_visited_set_keyed_by_name`.

For random pairs of programs that differ in one function, a function with the same code as written and the same recorded digests in both has the same optimized code in both.

For random small graphs with random bounding facts, every accepted graph, each fact's block forced through its exit once its bound is used up, has only finite paths (checked by brute force over every state).

For random small call graphs with random effect sources and random declarations.

- **`clones_never_share_a_feature_set`** *tested* (`crates/target-features/src/multiversion.rs`): no two clones of a plan have one feature set, and none has the unit's, so the baseline and the clones are compiled with pairwise different sets and (their feature names being part of an instance's shape) never share a code identity.

### v2

- **`a_function_of_the_build_is_one_request_however_a_body_names_it`** *tested* (`crates/hir-ty-codegen/v2/release.rs`): a release compile asks for each function of the build once, whatever the bodies it is made of call it: a request of an import's body whose target among the compile's references is one the compile already asks for, with the same signature, is that request. The import's body is linked under the first request of its function ([`emit`]), so a call through a second would be of a declaration LLVM has no body of, and whether there is a second follows from which crate each body was compiled in (the first asker's of the walk), which no key of the compile holds: the store then held one key's code two ways (`BLAZE_VERIFY_STORE`, 2026-11-11: `alloc::vec::from_elem::<u8>` built `RawVecInner::try_allocate_in` in at both of its calls in one program's unit and at one of them in another's).
  Controls: `a_request_kept_apart_by_its_name`.

## Reference models

### blaze-codegen

- **`level_walk`** (`crates/blaze-codegen/src/driver/tests/walk.rs`): the walk by levels that the worklist replaced. The roots are the first level (functions, then statics); each level is described in its order, its functions before its statics, and what a describe refers to that no level held yet is appended to the next, in its references' order. The functions and the statics, each in the order described.
- **`reached`** (`crates/blaze-codegen/src/driver/worklist/tests.rs`): what `roots` reach in `edges`, one node at a time.

### blaze-core

- **`Model`** (`crates/blaze-core/src/wheel.rs`): every timer with its deadline and insertion number, fired by sorting.

### blaze-diff

- **`saturation_is_no_dearer_than_naive_rewriting`** (`crates/blaze-diff/src/tests/simplify.rs`): equality saturation that ran to the end finds a term at most as dear as naive rewriting to a fixpoint does, since every term naive rewriting reaches is in the root's class, and extraction takes the cheapest of the class.

### blaze-ext-host

- **`reference`** (`crates/blaze-ext-host/src/facts/tests.rs`): every item from its bottom, whole sweeps until one changes nothing. No components, no order, no cache: the least fixpoint by its definition.

### blaze-hub

- **`Files`** (`crates/blaze-hub/src/tests.rs`): a tree is a flat map from each file's path to its mode and bytes, with no directories of its own; a path is a directory while some file is under it.

### blaze-link

- **`DebugProgram`** (`crates/blaze-link/src/beside/tests.rs`): a program is its functions by number; what a debugger sees of it is what [`inside`] reads of its debug info made whole.
- **`Program`** (`crates/blaze-link/src/tests/patch.rs`): a program is its functions by name and its statics' values; what it does is what [`normal`] reads of a fresh link of it.

### blaze-query

- **`evaluate`** (`crates/blaze-query/src/db/tests/changed.rs`): every node's value from scratch.
- **`model`** (`crates/blaze-query/src/tests/restore.rs`): what [`Double`] of file `file` is over `files`, from the files alone.

### blaze-usercode

- **`model`** (`crates/blaze-usercode/src/provider.rs`): the byte at `offset` of what `process` is given by `getrandom`, whatever anyone asked before.

### hir-ty-mir

- **`model_is_acyclic`** (`crates/hir-ty-mir/src/tests/consteval/reach.rs`): `S{root}` can own itself when some cell it owns (at any depth) owns (at any depth) a counted pointer whose pointee owns (at any depth) an `S{root}`. An explicit search with no pruning and no position flag, over the same description.
